cases.name: no body, no from — nothing to scan
ordinary benign email produces no signals
args: Thanks for your order, here is your receipt.

cases.name: single urgency phrase stays at low severity
args: Please act now to keep your account.

signals.label: Urgency / Pressure Language
signals.detail: Contains phrases designed to rush you past thinking it through: "act now". Manufactured time pressure is the most consistent feature of phishing.

cases.name: three or more urgency phrases escalate to medium severity
args: Your account will be suspended if you do not act now. This is your last warning.

signals.label: Urgency / Pressure Language
signals.detail: Contains phrases designed to rush you past thinking it through: "act now", "account will be suspended", "last warning". Manufactured time pressure is the most consistent feature of phishing.

cases.name: credential request phrase
args: Please enter your password to continue.

signals.label: Credential Request
signals.detail: Asks for login credentials or personal verification: "enter your password". Legitimate organizations do not ask you to confirm a password by email.

cases.name: financial request phrase
args: Please send payment via wire transfer today.

signals.label: Financial Request
signals.detail: References payment, transfer, or a change to financial details: "wire transfer". Changed banking details arriving by email is the core of invoice fraud.

cases.name: authority impersonation and secrecy request
args: This is your CEO, please keep this confidential.

signals.label: Authority Impersonation / Secrecy Request
signals.detail: Claims executive or IT authority, or asks you to keep it quiet: "this is your ceo", "keep this confidential". A request for secrecy exists to stop you verifying it through a second channel.

cases.name: generic greeting
args: Dear Customer, please review your statement.

signals.label: Generic Greeting
signals.detail: Addresses you generically rather than by name. An organization that holds an account for you generally knows your name.

cases.name: display name claims a known brand the actual address doesn't contain

signals.label: Display Name Spoofing
signals.detail: The sender name says "paypal" but the actual address is security@totally-different-domain.tk. Most mail clients show only the name, so this is what the recipient sees.

cases.name: display name is itself an address at a different domain — produces both the brand spoof and the address spoof signal

signals.label: Display Name Spoofing
signals.detail: The sender name says "paypal" but the actual address is attacker@evil.tk. Most mail clients show only the name, so this is what the recipient sees.

signals.label: Sender Address Spoofing
signals.detail: The display name shows an address at "paypal.com", but the message was actually sent from "evil.tk".

cases.name: excessive capitalization also incidentally hits the urgency phrase list ('urgent')
args: THIS IS AN URGENT ALERT ABOUT YOUR ACCOUNT NOW PLEASE READ CAREFULLY

signals.label: Urgency / Pressure Language
signals.detail: Contains phrases designed to rush you past thinking it through: "urgent". Manufactured time pressure is the most consistent feature of phishing.

signals.label: Excessive Capitalization
signals.detail: Unusually heavy use of all-caps words, typically used to manufacture alarm.
